# A clone descriptor is silently inert on a non-reactive config, which has no other protection from sharing

## Context

Filed after @tobiu dropped two PRs of mine (#18190, #18191) for fixing a symptom in `grid/Body.mjs` instead of proving what the class config system does. He was right on both counts, and his framing — *static config values get applied on instance level* — is correct and is half of the finding. This ticket is the other half, measured at `core.Base` with no grid involved.

## What was measured

A probe class, two instances, nothing else:

```javascript
class Probe extends core.Base {
    static config = {
        className     : 'Test.Unit.Core.Probe',
        plainArray    : [0, 0],
        reactiveArray_: [0, 0]
    }
}
```

| reading | `plainArray` (non-reactive) | `reactiveArray_` (reactive) |
|---|---|---|
| `Object.hasOwn(a, key)` | **true** | false (accessor) |
| `a[key] === b[key]` | **true** | false |
| `a[key] === Probe.config[key]` | **true** | — |
| after `a[key][0] = 99`, `b[key]` | **`[99,0]`** | `[0,0]` |
| after that write, `Probe.config[key]` | **`[99,0]`** | — |

Two facts, both true at once, which is why this was easy to argue past:

1. **The value IS applied at instance level.** `Object.hasOwn` returns `true`. Nothing is falling back to a prototype.
2. **The value is the class's own `static config` object.** `core.Base#mergeConfig()` ends with `return {...staticConfig, ...config}` — a shallow spread — and `processConfigs()` then does a plain `me[key] = me[configSymbol][key]`. Each instance gets its own property slot holding the same reference.

The consequence is worse than cross-instance sharing: the first in-place write **permanently corrupts the class default**, so every instance created afterwards starts from the mutated value.

## The actual defect

`learn/guides/fundamentals/DeclarativeConfigMerging.md` §Prototype Pollution documents the sharing and prescribes the remedy:

> To prevent this, **always** use `clone: 'deep'`

**That remedy does not reach a non-reactive config.** Same probe, with the documented descriptor applied to both a non-reactive and a reactive key:

| declaration | `a === b` | `b` after `a[0] = 99` |
|---|---|---|
| `clonedPlain` + `{[isDescriptor]: true, clone: 'deep', value: [0,0]}` | **true** | **`[99,0]`** |
| `clonedReactive_` + the identical descriptor | false | `[0,0]` |

The descriptor is accepted without error, warning, or effect. The `clone` switch that honours it lives inside the generated reactive setter (`src/Neo.mjs:430`), and a key without a trailing underscore never reaches a setter.

So a non-reactive config declared with a mutable literal has **no available protection at all** — not by default, and not by the mechanism the guide tells authors to reach for. The failure is silent in both directions: the sharing is silent, and the fix for it is silently ignored.

## Why this matters beyond one class

`src/grid/Body.mjs` declared `mountedRows`, `visibleRows` and `visibleColumns` this way and wrote through them by index. On a page with two grids the smaller grid's window overwrote the larger one's, and every row outside the borrowed window silently stopped repainting — the store stayed correct, so only the paint was missing. That was the symptom that led here, and it is one instance of the class, not the class itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a `clone` descriptor on a non-reactive config either takes effect, or is rejected loudly at `Neo.setupClass()` time. Silently accepting a no-op protection is the defect; either resolution closes it, and the choice between them is the design question this ticket exists to settle.
- [ ] **AC-2** — red-first: a spec at `test/playwright/unit/core/` demonstrates, against current `dev`, that two instances of a class with a non-reactive mutable config share one object, and that an in-place write through one reaches both the sibling instance **and** `ctor.config`.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the reactive case is asserted in the same file as the positive control, so the arms cannot pass by the config system doing nothing at all.
- [ ] **AC-4** — whichever resolution AC-1 takes, `DeclarativeConfigMerging.md` §Prototype Pollution states which config kinds `clone` applies to. The guide currently reads as though it applies to all of them.
- [ ] **AC-5** — no change to reactive-config behaviour, asserted by the existing suite staying green (3120 at time of filing).

## Out of Scope

- **Cloning every mutable non-reactive config by default.** That adds a clone to every instantiation of every class on a hot path (`Neo.create`), and I have not measured the cost. If it turns out to be the right answer it needs its own benchmark, not a side effect of this ticket.
- **`src/grid/Body.mjs`.** Its three windows are not configuration at all — nothing in `src/`, `apps/`, `examples/` or `test/` ever passes them as instance config — so that class wants instance fields regardless of how this ticket resolves. Separate lane, and not a reason to hold this one.
- A repo-wide sweep for other non-reactive mutable configs. Worth doing once the protection story is settled, so the sweep has something to recommend.

## Avoided Traps

- **Fixing it where it hurt.** Two PRs did that already and were correctly dropped. The grid was one caller.
- **Calling the shallow spread the bug.** It is documented behaviour with a documented opt-out. The bug is that the opt-out does not work where the guide says to use it.
- **Asserting isolation as the expected behaviour without deciding AC-1 first.** If the answer is "reject loudly", a test demanding isolation would encode the wrong contract.

## Related

- `src/Neo.mjs:430` — the `clone` switch, inside the reactive setter

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-03T11:10:18Z

`[PROVISIONAL_UNGRADUATED: D#18195]`

@tobiu classified config-system defects as prio 0 and routed the design question to the Ideation Sandbox. This ticket stays open as the defect record; the **shape of the fix is not settled here** — it is diverging in D#18195 with five live options and no fold marker.

Per `ticket-create-workflow.md §1d`, this marker stays until the Discussion reaches quorum. PR #18194 carries only the witness (`test.fail()` arms stating the contract the guides promise) and deliberately implements none of the options.

**Two of this ticket's own ACs already moved**, measured and posted on the Discussion:

- **AC on existing declarations — answered: zero.** No declaration in `src/` carries `clone` on a genuinely non-reactive key. The two candidates a sweep surfaced (`app/content/Container.mjs`, `app/content/PageContainer.mjs`, both `items`) inherit reactivity from `container/Base.mjs`'s `items_`; a subclass redeclaring a parent's reactive key *without* the underscore stays reactive, proved by probe. They are the guide's own worked example behaving correctly.
- **The occurrence count is not statically determinable.** A raw sweep gives 372 underscore-less mutable-literal configs in `src/`, and the number is unusable: a declaration site cannot tell you whether a key is reactive, because a parent may have made it so and `Neo.setupClass()` strips underscores from `ctor.config` anyway. That reshapes the question and is the point I most want peers to attack, since a detect-and-warn resolution that cannot be implemented statically is a different proposal than the one on the table.

AC-1 as filed ("either it takes effect, or it is rejected loudly") still stands as the minimum bar, and both remain open in the matrix alongside three others.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-03T18:19:32Z

Closing — the premise is a misquote of mine.

I built this ticket on *"always use `clone: 'deep'`"* from `DeclarativeConfigMerging.md` and cut the clause that scopes it. In full: *"always use `clone: 'deep'` **when using the Structural Injection Pattern with object-based items**"* — and `items` is reactive. Two sentences earlier the same guide says descriptors are how *"a parent class defines a **reactive config**"*; `ConfigSystem.md` says the same.

So a `clone` descriptor on a non-reactive key does nothing because **descriptors are a reactive-config mechanism**. Author category error, not silent inertness by the engine. There is no defect here, and AC-1's fork — "either it takes effect, or it is rejected loudly" — is a choice between two fixes for a thing that is not broken.

PR #18194 is closed for the same reason: it pinned three consequences of documented design as if they were latent bugs, which would have gone red on a legitimate future change and blocked it.

**What was real and already shipped:** `grid.Body` declared mutable per-instance state as non-reactive configs. That was an author error in `grid/Body`, fixed by #18202 by moving those keys onto the reactive path where descriptors work. It stands on its own.

@neo-opus-grace spent hours probing against this premise on D#18195 — the lost-notification hazard, the three-state pin matrix, the `merge: 'deep'` sweep. That work was real and the premise it served was not. She owns the Discussion follow-up; I am not opening anything new.
